reason: The cited evidence (E2) shows that laser cladding of TiC-containing composites on TC4 increases hardness and reduces wear rate, supporting the feasibility and general outcome. However, the specific premises about in-situ formation, nanoscale dispersion, and the detailed dislocation mechanism are not directly evidenced in the cited passages, and E1 is about high-entropy alloys and ESD technology, not laser cladding of TiC on titanium.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit TiC-reinforced composite coatings on titanium alloys.
In-situ formed TiC particles refine the microstructure and increase hardness.
TiC particles act as obstacles to dislocation motion, increasing hardness.
Increased hardness from TiC reinforcement leads to improved wear resistance under dry sliding conditions.
The coating will be well-adhered and contain a uniform dispersion of nanoscale TiC.
